KeyDifference: Establishes the theoretically-grounded 'learning to defer' (L2D) framework the modern sub-literature is built on; still a single binary classify-or-defer decision per item, trained end-to-end, with no multi-tier cascade, no dual independently-tracked confidence signals, no design-time whole-architecture-selection step, and no permanent-promotion-on-correction mechanism.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Foundational paper the entire modern L2D sub-literature builds on (Verma & Nalisnick 2022, Keswani et al. 2021, Liu et al. 2022 all extend it) -- establishes 'defer decisions informed by past expert behavior' is a mature (2020+), heavily-elaborated research program, but none of its extensions found add a design-time architecture-selection layer or a T4-to-T1-style permanent per-item promotion; that specific combination appears to be an actual gap in this literature.

Paper: Human-in-the-loop machine learning: a state of the art
Problem: Survey: taxonomizes active learning, interactive ML, machine teaching, curriculum learning, explainable AI as HITL ML
DecisionTarget: Varies (label-query targets, training curricula, etc.), not architecture selection
HumanDeferral: Central topic, but framed as human-in-the-TRAINING-loop, not human-in-the-inference-loop escalation
KeyDifference: This survey's HITL is almost entirely about the TRAINING process (active learning query strategies, machine teaching, curriculum design) -- a different lifecycle phase than ADS-Cascade's Part 2, which is inference-time human correction feeding back into a historical KB that changes future routing, not model retraining per se.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Useful for terminology-variant coverage but doesn't directly anticipate ADS-Cascade's specific mechanism (T4 manual entry permanently promoting to T1). Confirms 'human correction improves future system behavior' is a broad, well-established genre, but the specific implementation isn't described here.

Paper: Towards Unbiased and Accurate Deferral to Multiple Experts
Problem: Deferral to multiple experts with bias correction
HistoricalEvidence: Yes (historical expert predictions/labels as training signal)
KeyDifference: Extends L2D to multiple experts with fairness/bias correction; still a single deferral decision per item without ADS-Cascade's tiered structure, dual-signal tracking, or design-time historical-determinism-driven architecture choice.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Reinforces that 'who to defer to' and expert-bias correction are studied, but not the specific 4-tier + permanent-promotion mechanism.

Paper: Calibrated Learning to Defer with One-vs-All Classifiers
Problem: Calibration fix to Mozannar & Sontag's L2D parameterization
HistoricalEvidence: Yes (same expert-decision-history training signal as the L2D lineage)
KeyDifference: A calibration fix to the L2D framework; same limitations relative to ADS-Cascade as Mozannar & Sontag 2020 -- single defer decision, no design-time architecture selection, no permanent-promotion mechanism.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Shows the L2D literature is still actively iterating on calibration mechanics as of 2022 without ever reaching ADS-Cascade's specific combination.

Paper: Incorporating uncertainty in learning to defer algorithms for safe computer-aided diagnosis
Problem: Uncertainty-aware L2D loss for safe computer-aided diagnosis
EvidenceSignal: Two related uncertainty terms from the SAME model (prediction uncertainty + an epistemic-style term)
OverlapType: Partial overlap (strongest single adversarial hit for the dual-signal claim)
KeyDifference: Uses two related uncertainty terms from the SAME model to modulate ONE binary deferral decision -- a partial precedent for 'more than one confidence signal informing routing,' but not architecturally-separate OCR-confidence-vs-classification-confidence channels; still binary, not 4-tier; no design-time architecture-selection.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: STRONGEST single piece of adversarial evidence found anywhere in the sweep for the 'two independently-tracked confidence signals' claim -- ADS-Cascade must clearly distinguish 'OCR-confidence vs. classification-confidence, never blended' (architecturally separate channels) from 'prediction uncertainty + epistemic uncertainty from the same model' (this paper's approach).

Paper: Taxonomy of hybrid architectures involving rule-based reasoning and machine learning in clinical decision systems: A scoping review
Problem: Scoping review: 5 archetypes for combining rules and ML in clinical decision systems
HistoricalEvidence: Varies by reviewed system; no unifying determinism-style metric
DecisionTarget: Architecture pattern for combining rules and ML (5 archetypes)

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Weakens novelty of 'hybrid rule+ML architecture chosen at design time' as a general idea (71+ prior systems reviewed), but does not anticipate the specific determinism-score mechanism.

DecisionTarget: Which LLM(s) to call and in what order
KeyDifference: Unifies 'routing' (pick one model) and 'cascading' (escalate through models) into one theoretically optimal per-query framework, directly analogous in spirit to ADS-Cascade's T1-T4 tiers -- but purely runtime among LLMs of varying size, with no design-time dataset-level architecture-selection step, no rules-vs-ML distinction, no human-in-the-loop feedback.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Provides a more rigorous/optimal theoretical foundation for exactly the kind of confidence-gated escalation ADS-Cascade's Part 2 implements informally; ADS-Cascade's runtime cascade could be seen as a domain-specific, less formally optimal instance of this general pattern.

Paper: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
Problem: Query-difficulty-routed small/large LLM selection
HistoricalEvidence: Yes (router trained on historical query/quality data)
DecisionTarget: Small model vs. large model per query
ThresholdCalibration: Learned (tunable quality-level dial at test time)
KeyDifference: Two-tier confidence/difficulty-gated routing between cheap/expensive models, structurally similar to a subset of ADS-Cascade's tiers, but purely runtime, no design-time phase, both tiers are LLMs rather than rules/embedding/LLM.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Reinforces that confidence-gated tiered LLM routing at runtime is a well-established, highly-cited (377 citations) pattern -- the runtime half of ADS-Cascade is not architecturally novel in isolation.

Paper: Optimising Calls to Large Language Models with Uncertainty-Based Two-Tier Selection
Problem: Uncertainty-based two-tier small/large LLM selection (no extra neural router)
HistoricalEvidence: No (uncertainty of small-model generations only, no extra training)
DecisionTarget: Accept small-model output vs. escalate to large LLM
KeyDifference: Explicitly a 'two-tier' confidence-gated cascade (echoing ADS-Cascade's tier language) but confined to LLM-vs-LLM escalation with no rules layer, no design-time step, no human-feedback loop into historical data.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Minor -- narrow, LLM-only scope limits overlap, but shows 'two-tier confidence gating' terminology/pattern predates and is independent of ADS-Cascade.

Paper: Split Computing and Early Exiting for Deep Learning Applications: Survey and Research Challenges
Problem: Survey of split-computing and early-exit DNN methods
DecisionTiming: Both (exit points/thresholds fixed design-time; exit decision runtime)
HistoricalEvidence: No (thresholds tuned on held-out validation performance, not live historical label agreement)

DecisionTarget: Depth of computation per input (early exit vs. full pipeline)
KeyDifference: Early-exit is architecturally a tiered-confidence cascade resembling T1-T4 in SHAPE, but operates within a single DNN's layers on accuracy/latency, not across heterogeneous mechanism types (rules/embeddings/LLM), with no design-time dataset-level architecture-selection and no human-feedback loop.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Shows that 'tiered escalation gated by per-item confidence, with tier boundaries fixed in advance' is a long-established general ML pattern (early exiting), independent of ADS-Cascade's specific domain and metric.

Paper: Machine learning for financial transaction classification across companies using character-level word embeddings of text fields
Venue: Intelligent Systems in Accounting, Finance and Management, vol. 28(3)

HumanDeferral: Yes (top-5 suggestion list for accountant approval, by default, not confidence-tiered)

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Closest single B8 finding to ADS-Cascade's Part 1 cross-company-consistency design rule -- shows the underlying empirical justification (companies differ enough that global classifiers underperform) was already documented in 2021 in essentially the same application domain, weakening novelty of that specific threshold-driven design choice, though ADS-Cascade's determinism-score formalism and its extension to rules/LLM tiers go beyond this paper.

Paper: Detecting Anomalies in Financial Data Using Machine Learning Algorithms

HistoricalEvidence: Yes (real-life GL dataset, historical journal entries)

DesignTimeSelection: Not specified as a formal pre-deployment step

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Reinforces that Part 2 (confidence-tiered auto-apply/review, human corrections feeding back into the model) is now commodity/standard practice among AP-automation vendors -- weakens novelty claims for the runtime cascade specifically, while leaving Part 1 less directly challenged by this source.

HumanDeferral: Yes (explicit: route low-confidence cases to human review)
ClosestADSComponent: Part 2 + a loose Part 1 analog (operational baseline, not a label-consistency metric)
KeyDifference: Recommends measuring a current-state/historical baseline before deploying AI agents plus confidence-gated auto-post/review -- structurally similar in spirit but far less formal than ADS-Cascade's determinism-score-driven architecture decision; 'baseline' here is operational (time, exception counts), not a label-consistency metric.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Further corroborates that 'measure before you automate, then confidence-gate at runtime' is now widely articulated general AP-automation guidance across multiple vendors (Ramp, Peakflo, Ken From Finance) -- a pattern, if not a formal method.

Paper: Introduction to Information Retrieval (textbook, cluster purity, Ch. 16.3)
Problem: Defines cluster purity as an extrinsic clustering-evaluation metric
DecisionTiming: N/A (metric definition, not a decision procedure)

KeyDifference: purity(cluster) = max_j(class-j count)/(cluster size) is the IDENTICAL closed-form expression as ADS(p) = max(c_i)/sum(c_i), under 'cluster' <-> 'item's historical booking multiset.' Not an analogy -- the same formula, relabeled unit of analysis.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Directly challenges any claim that ADS's mathematical construction is novel. The metric itself is a ~2003-2009-documented, textbook-canonical clustering-evaluation statistic. Novelty must rest entirely on ADS's design-time architecture-selection APPLICATION, not the formula.

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Same as G1-01; additionally supplies a citable formal critique of the metric family's known weaknesses, relevant to ADS's own limitations discussion.

Paper: Criterion functions for document clustering / CLUTO lineage
Problem: Criterion-function formalization of clustering-evaluation metrics incl. purity
KeyDifference: Independent lineage (CLUTO toolkit) confirming the same formula's canonical status, separate from the IR-book/Amigo lineage.

Paper: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Observer Error-Rates Using the EM Algorithm
Venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Strongest evidence that ADS's exact quantity is a known baseline in the repeated-labeling literature -- just diffusely/informally named rather than anchored to one canonical citation the way ADS's paper could imply.

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Useful citation for justifying, not undermining, ADS's design choice to collapse to a scalar -- shows the field has explicitly debated this exact tradeoff.

PotentialChallengeToContribution: Minimal -- confirms convergent GOAL but not mathematical equivalence; worth citing as a contrast, not a match.

KeyDifference: Same OPERATOR (max of a probability-like distribution) as ADS but applied to a model's live predictive distribution, not an empirical historical frequency distribution -- structurally analogous, mathematically Distinct input.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Minimal direct challenge; valuable as a precise contrast citation (same operator, different data) rather than a competing claim.

But the informal 'percent agreement with the majority label' construct that circulates in this same literature IS mathematically equivalent to ADS -- and, like G1-04, has no dedicated citation of its own distinct from kappa.
PotentialChallengeToContribution: Most important 'near miss' in the gap pass: confirms the raw majority-agreement-proportion genuinely lacks its own canonical citation lineage, exactly as suspected before this search was run.
